title: Multimodal & Voice AI Systems

requirements.title: Explicit opt-in ephemeral BYOK live mode
Python engineering standard and fail-fast gates
Built-in reviewer guidance in the UI

adrs.title: Separate presentation from authoritative application logic
Deterministic and live modes are first-class execution modes
Real streaming requires a real WebSocket boundary
External and model-derived content is untrusted
Cost and latency are architectural concerns

evidence_classes.meaning: Architecture, contracts, and documentation. Proves design intent only.
Automated tests executed against deterministic code paths.
Reviewer-run workflow using deterministic adapters, no external key.
Workflow executed against a real external provider with opt-in credentials.
Packaged, deployed, or released artifact exercised in its target environment.

security_invariants.title: Untrusted multimodal input separation
security_invariants.control: TrustLevel on every ModalityInput; external inputs cannot be APPLICATION; transcripts, history, and replies are untrusted (9.6)

security_invariants.title: MIME/type validation
security_invariants.control: Per-modality media type allowlist in ModalityInput

security_invariants.title: Extension/content consistency
security_invariants.control: Extension must match media type (contract); magic-byte and UTF-8 text check at ingestion (9.3, image and document); audio signature check and strict RIFF/WAVE parsing (9.4)

security_invariants.title: Safe filename/path handling
security_invariants.control: display_name rejects separators, traversal, control chars; content held by opaque reference

security_invariants.title: File-size limits
security_invariants.control: Per-modality hard byte ceilings; configurable ResourceBudget below ceilings

security_invariants.title: Audio-duration limits
security_invariants.control: Audio inputs require duration_ms within ceiling; duration measured from the WAV header and checked against the session budget before decoding (9.4)

security_invariants.title: Bounded document processing
security_invariants.control: Page-count ceiling and size ceiling for documents; page budget checked before PDF extraction; extracted text and sections bounded (9.3)

security_invariants.title: Malformed/unsupported input rejection
security_invariants.control: Strict models (extra=forbid); unknown modality/type/event rejected; malformed, truncated, and unsupported audio rejected (9.4); malformed, unknown, server-only, binary, and extra-field client messages and non-canonical base64 audio rejected with safe protocol errors, and repeated protocol errors end the session (9.7)

security_invariants.title: Prompt-injection containment
security_invariants.control: Untrusted content is data in the reasoning context, never instructions or tool authority; each observation is a JSON-encoded part beside a fixed application task, and reasoning output is citation-checked before it is recorded (9.5); voice turns carry the transcript as one JSON-encoded part and history as untrusted turns beside a fixed task, and every reply act is citation-checked before it is spoken or committed (9.6)

security_invariants.title: No arbitrary command execution
security_invariants.control: No shell/subprocess/eval path; provider ports expose no tool execution

security_invariants.title: No authority from model/provider/content output
security_invariants.control: Provider results are UNTRUSTED_MODEL_OUTPUT; mode, budgets, credentials set only by application config; transcripts tested as inert data (9.4); turn requests carry no mode, budget, provider, or evidence fields and the session configuration is bound when application code opens the conversation (9.6); client messages carry no session, mode, budget, provider, trust, or evidence field, session IDs are server-generated and bound to the connection, and turn events carry server-authored classifications only (9.7)

security_invariants.title: Provider/network trust boundaries
security_invariants.control: Only live adapters cross the network boundary; deterministic adapters make no network calls

security_invariants.title: Outbound provider allowlisting
security_invariants.control: SessionConfig.allowed_live_providers allowlist (empty by default); endpoints from committed allowlisted config only; the OpenAI adapters use one fixed endpoint with no base-URL setting (9.8)

security_invariants.title: Bounded payloads
security_invariants.control: Text, delta, transcript, and stream message size bounds; client message, decoded audio, reply fragment, per-turn event, protocol-frame, and connection bounds enforced by the WebSocket gateway, with compression off and a bounded inbound frame queue (9.7)

security_invariants.title: Timeout behavior
security_invariants.control: ResourceBudget.request_timeout_s and session_timeout_s ceilings; local decoding bounded by request_timeout_s (9.3); audio decoding and every speech provider call bounded by request_timeout_s (9.4); voice-turn reasoning bounded by request_timeout_s and sessions closed after session_timeout_s (9.6); streamed reasoning bounded by a request deadline, and every WebSocket send, idle connection, and streamed turn bounded by a timeout (9.7)

security_invariants.title: Bounded retry behavior
security_invariants.control: ResourceBudget.max_retries ceiling of 3

security_invariants.title: No uncontrolled retry loops
security_invariants.control: Retries count against max_provider_calls_per_session; no unbounded loops; each voice turn reserves its provider calls up front and failed turns are not refunded (9.6); live clients use max_retries=0 and each live adapter instance has a provider-call budget (9.8)

security_invariants.title: Secret redaction
security_invariants.control: Credentials are SecretStr, excluded from serialization and repr; provider errors translated to fixed messages without chaining; central redaction and logging filter (9.8)

security_invariants.title: No secrets in logs, traces, evidence, URLs, source control, or committed config
security_invariants.control: Credentials never in models that are logged or emitted; .env ignored; tests scan emitted payloads

security_invariants.title: Explicit opt-in live credentials
security_invariants.control: LIVE mode requires live_opt_in=True and a credential; credential presence alone never selects LIVE; services reach live adapters only for explicit live sessions and explicit live bindings, with no fallback (9.8)

security_invariants.title: Ephemeral user-supplied credentials
security_invariants.control: Credentials held in session memory only; never persisted; passed explicitly to a per-call client that is closed after the call (9.8)

security_invariants.title: No unnecessary retention of sensitive content
security_invariants.control: Opaque references with session-scoped lifetime; deletion at session end; Story 9.3 and 9.4 uploads and generated audio released before the call returns; voice conversations retain bounded text only and release it when the session closes (9.6); WebSocket sessions are closed and released when the connection ends, and audio payloads are never echoed (9.7)

security_invariants.title: Safe structured errors
security_invariants.control: SafeError(code, message, retryable) with bounded message; no stack traces or secrets; unexpected gateway failures are logged server-side and reach the client only as a fixed internal_error (9.7)

security_invariants.title: Testable expected failure paths
security_invariants.control: Every rejection path has an automated test

security_invariants.title: Accurate evidence classification
security_invariants.control: EvidenceRecord validators prevent weaker evidence claiming stronger class

security_invariants.title: Fail closed when trust or validation is uncertain
security_invariants.control: Unknown types, missing duration, invalid mode, malformed events are rejected, not defaulted

definition_of_done: Every authoritative source requirement is traced.
The voice-enabled AI assistant is demonstrable.
The integrated multimodal AI platform works.
Live BYOK mode is explicit opt-in and safely bounded.
The UI includes concise built-in reviewer/user guidance.
Security and failure paths are tested.
Structured observability exists without secret leakage.
Documentation, type, and error-handling standards are satisfied.
Architecture, ADRs, requirements, traceability, project status, and README accurately describe the implementation.
